rationale: Constellation shows 10/20/30mm graphite all give near-identical hotspot (~325K) with large margin to 340K limit, suggesting spreading is already saturated at 10mm (kt=1.5) and thickness can shrink to cut mass. Graphite has the best density/conductivity ratio (1800/150=12) of all tested materials, so testing the thinnest plausible plate first.
Same saturation evidence as above; bracketing 1mm with a slightly thicker option in case 1mm is below the spreading threshold.
Bracketing candidate between 2mm and 5mm to refine where hotspot departs from the ~325K saturated value seen at 10-30mm in the constellation.
Half the thickness of the cheapest known all-PASS design (10mm graphite, mass 18 kg/m2); tests whether the flat hotspot trend (325K at 10/20/30mm) extends down to 5mm.
Intermediate point between 5mm and the known-good 10mm graphite baseline, for bracketing the saturation/threshold boundary.

Aluminium's 10/20/30mm hotspots are also flat at ~324K; aluminium's density/conductivity ratio (13.5) is close to graphite's (12), so thin aluminium is a cross-check on whether the saturation behavior generalizes across materials rather than being graphite-specific.
Bracketing point above 2mm for aluminium, same saturation-boundary rationale as the graphite series.
Further bracketing point for aluminium approaching half of the known 10mm all-PASS design mass (27 kg/m2).

Copper's high conductivity (400 W/mK) means even 1mm gives kt=0.4, comparable to thin graphite/aluminium candidates, testing whether high-k thin copper is competitive on mass (density 8960) despite its poor density/conductivity ratio (22.4).
Bracketing point above 1mm copper to see the local trend for a high-conductivity, high-density material at low thickness.
